title: PR #36990 added the support app's CourseTeamManageAPIView with only IsAuthenticated, without the support-role gate every sibling support view uses, so any learner can probe arbitrary accounts and instructors can read other users' course roles.

findings.explanation: No SQL queries are constructed or executed in this diff. The code uses Django ORM serializers and model methods, which handle parameterization automatically.

The diff shows URL routing and test cases for a CourseTeamManageAPIView endpoint, but the actual view implementation is not included. Tests reference authorization checks (e.g., instructors seeing only their courses), but without seeing the actual view code, it's impossible to verify if authorization is properly enforced. The tests suggest role-based access control exists, but the underlying implementation is missing from this diff.

evidence.content:
def test_get_api_instructor_can_only_see_their_courses(self):
        """GET API: Course instructor sees only courses they have access to."""
        self.client.login(
            username=self.instructor_user.username, password=TEST_PASSWORD
        )
        resp = self.client.get(self.url, {"email": self.user.email})
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)

        course_ids = [course["course_id"] for course in resp.data]
        self.assertIn(str(self.extra_courses[0].id), course_ids)
        for i in range(1, 3):
            self.assertNotIn(str(self.extra_courses[i].id), course_ids)

findings.suggested_fix: Review the actual view implementation (not shown in this diff) to ensure: (1) authorization checks are performed before returning course data, (2) users can only access courses they have explicit roles in, (3) GET requests with email parameters validate that the requesting user has permission to view that user's course roles, (4) PUT requests validate that the requesting user has permission to modify roles in the specified courses.
